headline: Models infer transcriptomic, protein and 3D tissue state directly from H&E and coarse spatial data
label: Histology To Spatial Omics Inference
summary: Several preprints within one week extend H&E-to-omics prediction to 1,000-gene panels, single-cell RNA and protein, and 3D tissue reconstruction.
synthesis: The dominant thread is predicting molecular state from histology or lower-resolution spatial measurements. GeneFlow applies flow matching to panels of up to 1,000 genes; SCOPE adds RNA-protein biomarker priors for single-cell RNA and protein prediction across 16 organs; Loki2 is a single-cell pathology foundation model trained on 15M cells with morphology-linked latents; GenVinci, trained on 300M profiles, reconstructs 3D tissue from H&E and maps senescence. sc-HistoMorphomics links 194 nuclear features to spatial transcriptomics. A related strand increases resolution within spatial data: st2sc infers single-cell expression from multicellular spots, SpOTr uses Fused Gromov-Wasserstein transport with deconvolution, and a rotation-equivariant network infers 3D cell shape from transcript point clouds. ST-FateFlow extends flow matching to time-resolved spatial data. Other items on metacells, domain detection and regulatory networks are adjacent.
